source.title: Information Flow Routes: Automatically Interpreting Language Models at Scale

page_placements.theme: Previous-token heads: generic role, consistent timing, data dependence

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies information-flow routes and previous-token heads, but does not identify induction heads, test their [A][B] … [A] → [B] behavior, or investigate their formation during training or their role in in-context learning.
record.gate_note: The paper reports findings about previous-token heads, which are related to one component named in V1, but does not test whether they compose into induction heads or produce induction behavior. The reported head-importance results are recorded under fits_no_version. Its training, phase-change, in-context-learning, and few-shot-learning discussion is not experimental evidence about the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces an attribution-based information-flow method and reports that previous-token heads are important in GPT2-Small (IOI) and Llama 2-7B (C4). It never identifies induction heads, tests [A][B]…[A]→[B] behaviour, tracks training dynamics, or measures in-context learning, so no version is tested. The record's 'discusses' is generous: induction heads are not mentioned. 'cites_only' (Elhage et al. 2021 is cited for 'residual stream') would also be defensible.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that attribution-based information-flow routes recover patching circuits about 100x faster and are more versatile. They also report that Llama 2 has generally important previous-token and subword-merging heads, POS-dependent flow patterns, and domain-specialized components. They draw no conclusion about induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses attribution-based information-flow routes rather than an induction-head identification or training-time measurement procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: Previous-token heads appear in GPT2-Small IOI routes for both original and contrastive templates, so they are not IOI-specific (Figure 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Previous-token heads are generic components active across predictions, not task-specific.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama 2-7B on C4, several previous-token heads exist, and almost all are the most important heads in their layers (Figure 9a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Previous-token heads are among the most generally important attention heads in large LMs.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), 2024
record.problems: The reported relevant head-importance values are shown in figures without numerical values in the text. The paper does not measure induction behavior or training-time formation.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included: the remaining analyses concern information-flow routes, POS patterns, subword-merging heads, domains, or other tasks, not induction-head behavior or the claim's predicted training and in-context-learning effects.

untested.parts: Whether previous-token heads compose with later induction heads and whether those heads implement [A][B]…[A]→[B]; no attention-only models studied.
No training checkpoints; no formation timing, abruptness, or loss bump.
No in-context learning measure (loss vs token index) and no induction-head attribution.
No induction heads identified in GPT2-Small, OPT-125m or Llama 2-7B.
No manipulation of training data or setup.

record.verdict_notes: The study's only overlap with the claim is that it finds previous-token heads, the upstream component named in V1. Their importance is reported in figures only, and no composition with induction heads is tested. A previous-token head is defined as one that puts more than half its influence on the previous token in at least 70% of cases.

versions.untested_parts: Whether induction heads form by composing with previous-token heads and implement the stated copying behavior.
Induction-head formation over training time, abruptness, timing relative to in-context learning, and the training-loss bump.
Whether induction heads carry most in-context learning in large transformers.
Induction behavior across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
Whether training data or setup changes induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Whether few-shot task learning is mainly carried by mechanisms other than induction heads.
Whether induction-head formation consists of multiple sub-steps or overlapping transitions.
